I'm looking for plus-shaped clusters of zeros - a center cell with all four neighbors also zero - and marking them with color 3. Checking example 1 at rows 6-8 confirms this: the cells at (6,1),(7,0),(7,1),(7,2),(8,1) are all 0 in the input, forming exactly that plus pattern, and they get colored 3 in the output.

Example 3 shows overlapping pluses can share cells too, like at rows 9-11 where two pluses centered at (10,1) and (10,2) merge together, so I need to mark every cell belonging to any valid plus shape, even if shapes overlap. I don't see the actual test input grid yet, so I'll need to wait for it before applying this rule.

I'm scanning the grid row by row, checking each zero cell to see if its four neighbors (up, down, left, right) are also zero, which would mark it as the center of a plus shape.

Testing rows 1 through 4, I find one match so far: cell (2,5), since its neighbors up, down, left, and right are all zero. I continue checking remaining candidates in rows 3 and 4, but none qualify yet.

Moving to rows 5 and 6, I find another match at (5,9), where all four neighbors are zero. I continue scanning row 6's candidates, none of which qualify so far.

Working through rows 7 and 8, I check each zero cell's neighbors but keep hitting walls where at least one direction is 8, ruling them out.

In row 9, I find (9,1) satisfies the condition with all four neighbors zero, and I'm now checking (9,2) for the same pattern.

Continuing to row 10, I finish checking remaining candidates and confirm the final plus-shaped set: (2,5), (5,9), (9,1), (9,2). Now I'm marking these cells.
